clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: Which environmental action best supports fall prevention in a hospitalized client's room?

options.A: Keep the route to the bathroom and door clear of clutter, cords, equipment, and unstable furniture, with needed items placed safely within reach.
options.B: Store frequently used equipment along the walking route so staff can reach it quickly, then move it when the client needs to ambulate.
options.C: Leave electrical cords crossing the edge of the walking path when they are visible, because the client can step around them during ambulation.
options.D: Place personal items outside the client's easy reach and reduce room lighting so the client is encouraged to ask staff for help before moving.

semantic_correction.rationale: A is correct. Current AHRQ fall-prevention resources emphasize reducing environmental hazards by keeping pathways clear and removing clutter, electrical or telephone cords, unstable furniture, and other objects from walking areas. AHRQ also advises keeping the call light and personal items within easy reach so clients do not need to stretch, climb, or move unnecessarily to obtain them. In hospital fall-prevention programs, room-environment safety is combined with individualized risk assessment and tailored interventions. Therefore the safest environmental action is to maintain a clear, unobstructed walking path and safe access to needed items. B is incorrect because equipment in the walking route creates a trip hazard. C is incorrect because visible cords remain environmental hazards even when the client knows they are present. D is incorrect because poor lighting and inaccessible items can increase fall risk rather than prevent it.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Reduce environmental fall risk by maintaining clear, unobstructed walking paths, removing clutter and cords, ensuring adequate lighting, and keeping needed items safely within reach.

audit_findings_append.finding: One clearly best environmental fall-prevention action with balanced alternatives and no absolute-word cue.

option_audit.A: Correct. It removes documented trip hazards and keeps needed items safely accessible.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Equipment stored in the walking route creates an avoidable obstruction.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Electrical cords crossing a walking path remain a trip hazard even when visible.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Poor lighting and inaccessible items can increase fall risk.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A uniquely removes environmental hazards; B-C introduce obstacles and D worsens visibility and access.
cueing_check: All four options are parallel environmental actions of comparable length and specificity; the prior absolute-word distractor was removed.
